What it is

Rebuild this animation 1:1: Lake's onboarding carousel - each page pairs a headline with a black-and-white line illustration that colorizes with a spreading watercolor paint effect as the page settles, so art arrives monochrome and blooms into color.

Media

Frame-by-frame

Build prompt

Rebuild this animation 1:1: Lake's onboarding carousel - each page pairs a headline with a black-and-white line illustration that colorizes with a spreading watercolor paint effect as the page settles, so art arrives monochrome and blooms into color.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
White onboarding pager: large square illustration upper half, headline + body copy below, page dots / next control at bottom. Three pages shown: a woman's face in dense florals ("Be kind to your mind"), objects on a shelf ("Make the world a better place"), a classical bust with rocket and clouds ("Let your creativity flow").

## Motion spec
Pattern: choreographed entrance on page change.
- Page transition: horizontal swipe between pages (~300ms, ease-out), standard pager behavior.
- On page settle, the illustration starts fully black-and-white line art.
- Color blooms in as soft watercolor washes: each region fills with an organic, slightly overspilling edge (paint bleed past the line art), staggered region by region over ~1.2-1.8s.
- Larger background washes first, small accents last; each fill eases opacity 0 -> 1 with a soft radial spread (~400ms per region, 80-120ms stagger).
- Headline and copy are static; only the illustration paints.

## Calibration
- The paint must feel wet: edges bleed outside the linework a few px, colors slightly desaturated like real watercolor.
- Stagger long enough to read as painting, not a crossfade.

## Reduced motion
Illustration crossfades from monochrome to full color (250ms) on page settle, no regional stagger.

## Don't miss
- Color overshoots the line boundaries - contained fills kill the effect.
- Each new page re-enters monochrome and repaints; the color is per-page, not remembered.
